text:
Sana: Heads up — we're bringing up OpenWeights-v2 (7.5B) for internal evals. I skimmed the repo license and there's a clause about redistribution + attribution that seems restrictive. Can we confirm whether we can ship quantized weights to customers? cc @Miguel @Liz
Miguel: Do you have the exact clause? there are subtle differences between 'redistribute' and 're-host' in these licenses.
Liz: If redistribution is allowed but attribution required, that's usually fine; problem is when they forbid commercial use or derivative weights.
Sana: Pasted the snippet below from LICENSE.md on the model repo:
```
Section 4. Redistribution: The model weights may be redistributed in source or binary form for non-commercial use only. Any redistribution must include prominent attribution to OriginalModelOrg and retain this license. Modified weights (including quantized or pruned variants) are considered derivative works and are subject to the same non-commercial restriction.
```
Sana: So it explicitly calls out quantized/pruned as derivative works.
Miguel: That sounds like a non-commercial clause. That would block shipping to paying customers.
Oliver: Is there any precedent for treating quantized weights as "tooling" vs "derivative"? we often consider quantization as a transformation, but legal might not.
Mika: From a product perspective, Dedicated/private customers expect to get weights for on-prem inference in some cases. If this is NC (non-commercial), it kills that.
Legal-Bot: Automated note: license contains "non-commercial" and "derivative" language. Recommend human review for commercial redistribution and attribution placement.
Sana: @Kelsey (Legal) can you advise whether we can (a) ship quantized weights to a paying customer under this license, and (b) if attribution in-app (UI footer) is sufficient?
Kelsey (Legal): Quick read: this is a copyleft-ish NC clause. Short answers: (a) No, the clause as written prohibits redistribution for commercial purposes, including providing weights to paying customers, whether quantized or not. (b) Attribution is required but doesn't cure the NC restriction.
Kelsey (Legal): Next steps: we can ask upstream for a commercial license or an exception for derivative artifacts (quantized weights). Request template I can send. Also check model provenance — if any third-party checkpoints were mixed in, that can complicate relicensing.
Miguel: For documentation: if we request an exception, we should propose: 1) allow redistribution of quantized/pruned variants for commercial use; 2) require attribution text: "Model derived from OriginalModelOrg OpenWeights-v2"; 3) retain a copy of the unmodified license in the artifact.
Liz: Also flag eval regressions — if we produce quantized variants for customers, we need to include the quantization config and a test suite so they can reproduce. This helps with trust and may make upstream more comfortable.
Oliver: Technical question: can we instead provide a hosted inference option (Redwood-hosted) that avoids shipping weights? would that satisfy legal?
Kelsey (Legal): Yes — offering inference as a service (no weights transferred) is typically within scope unless license expressly forbids commercial deployment. But here the license restricts redistribution; hosting should be fine, but confirm upstream's TOS for deployment.
Sana: Ok. Action items: (1) I'll open a request to upstream asking for a commercial redistribution addendum for quantized weights. (2) @Kelsey can you draft the request template and review provenance? (3) @Liz/Miguel/OIiver — prepare minimal quantization/docs/test artifacts to propose.
Mika: Adding: product needs timeline — if upstream declines, fall back plan is Redwood-hosted offering for enterprise customers.
Kelsey (Legal): I'll draft the request and post here in ~24h. Template will include suggested attribution language and a short commercial redistribution clause. :+1:
Sana: Thanks all. marking as blocker for Dedicated onboarding until we get an exception or confirm hosting-only path. :eyes:
